_doc: ESB project contract for the N-AALP public reference. gates[] are the executable acceptance gates a maintainer (and CI) runs; a required failure fails the build and writes honest evidence to .shippable/evidence/latest.json. Unlike a spec-only project, N-AALP grades its constructions by running code: two byte-identical reference implementations against independent non-circular oracles, the CDDL machine-validated, and ten SDKs graded against the shared conformance corpus. The spec-parity ledger (.shippable/spec-parity.json) records every construction and SDK with an honest status, owner, and gate.

gates.name: pins
gates.purpose: The canonical draft, CDDL, registries, and full conformance corpus are provably the exact bytes recorded in PIN.json + MANIFEST.sha256 (no drift).

gates.name: two-implementation-parity
gates.purpose: Go and Rust produce byte-identical CBOR, signed input, signatures, and digests, each cross-validated against the independent non-circular oracle; the committed vectors match the oracle output (no drift).

gates.name: cddl-conformance
gates.purpose: The full spec/naalp-draft-00.cddl is well-formed and validates the committed vectors against their production in the Bormann cddl tool (RFC 8610); cross-rule mismatches are rejected.

gates.name: registry-drift
gates.purpose: The machine-readable registries (signatures/multicodec/channels/protocols) stay consistent with the graded vectors.

gates.name: cross-language-conformance
gates.purpose: Every reference SDK adapter whose toolchain is present is graded against the shared op-replay corpus, and deterministic ML-DSA COSE_Sign1 is byte-identical across the crypto-capable languages. A present adapter that fails is a hard failure; an absent toolchain is an honest skip.

gates.name: conformance-master
gates.purpose: The single master gate composing the four above; the definition of 'the protocol is graded'.
